entities.name: Jaume de Prades i de Foix
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Jaume de Prades i de Foix (1341–1396), a prominent Aragonese nobleman, served the Crown of Aragon as Count of Prades, Baron of Entença, and a significant patron of the arts during the late 14th century. Born into the royal house as the son of Joan de Prades (half-brother to King Peter IV), his life spanned a period marked by dynastic rivalries, military campaigns against Castile, and the flourishing of Gothic culture within the Mediterranean sphere. His influence extended beyond mere noble titles, manifesting in his active military command, diplomatic missions, and most notably, his substantial patronage of religious institutions and artistic endeavors, particularly the Royal Monastery of Poblet, which solidified his legacy as a key figure in Aragonese cultural and political life.

Throughout his career, Jaume de Prades participated actively in the political and military affairs of the Crown of Aragon. He fought alongside King Peter IV in the War of the Two Peters (1356–1369) against Castile, demonstrating his military prowess and loyalty to the Aragonese crown. He also undertook diplomatic missions, such as his embassy to Paris in 1373 to negotiate with Charles V of France, reflecting his trusted position within the royal court. His most enduring contributions, however, centered on his extensive patronage of the arts and religious foundations. From 1383, he initiated significant architectural and artistic commissions at the Monastery of Poblet, including the construction of a new dormitory and the embellishment of the royal pantheon, transforming the Cistercian abbey into a vibrant cultural hub under his influence.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Jaume de Prades i de Foix's extensive patronage profoundly shaped the artistic and architectural development of the Royal Monastery of Poblet, cementing its role as a key cultural and spiritual center in the Crown of Aragon. His commissions left a lasting legacy of Gothic art and architecture.
